data.source_title: Discrete-event simulation and design of experiments to study ambulatory patient waiting time in an emergency department
data.locator: Table 5, statistical distributions of service times used in simulation; Table 1 and study description for sample/setting.
data.source_setting: Ambulatory emergency patients at a hospital ED in Quebec, Canada; physician/nurse/admin work and patient trajectories modeled.
data.source_period: One week of patient-flow data collection; exact calendar dates not reported in inspected article.
data.source_n: 1,035 ED arrivals observed during the collection week; 640 ambulatory patients (395 stretcher patients). Service-time fitting sample counts not given.
data.quantity: Triage service-time distribution used in the DES model
data.unit: minutes; parameter convention as printed in source
data.parameterization: LOGN(5.74, 3.816) min, reproduced as printed; source does not clearly state parameter convention in the table.
data.source_evidence_basis: The paper calls these statistical distributions used in the simulation; they are model inputs and should not be claimed as verified empirical fits absent a reported fitting procedure.
data.limitations: Single ED and ambulatory population; fit sample size and fitting method not reported; distribution parameter convention is under-specified. Not an RWJ observation.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Candidate external distribution for sensitivity only after resolving parameter convention; keep distinct from empirical mean data and do not treat as a local model default.

data.locator: Table 5, statistical distributions of service times used in simulation.

data.source_period: One week of patient-flow data collection; exact calendar dates not reported in inspected article.
data.source_n: 1,035 ED arrivals observed; 640 ambulatory patients. Registration-duration fitting sample count is not reported.
data.quantity: Registration service-time distribution used in the DES model
data.unit: minutes; triangular minimum, mode, maximum as listed by source
data.source_evidence_basis: Explicitly a distribution used in the simulation. The article does not state that this triangular input was empirically fitted; this record therefore labels it as a model assumption/input.

data.inferred_scenario_use: External model-input comparator for registration duration scenarios only; maintain the source's assumed status and do not present as an empirical distribution or RWJ timing.

data.source_title: Discrete-event simulation and design of experiments to study ambulatory patient waiting time in an emergency department
data.locator: Table 5, statistical distributions of service times used in the simulation model: consultation and second consultation.
data.source_setting: Ambulatory emergency patients at a hospital ED in Quebec, Canada; initial and return consultations modeled separately.
data.source_period: One week of patient-flow data collection; exact calendar dates not reported in inspected article.
data.source_n: 1,035 ED arrivals observed; 640 ambulatory patients. Consultation service-time sample counts are not reported.
data.quantity: Physician consultation service-time distributions used in DES
data.unit: minutes; triangular minimum, mode, maximum as listed by source
data.source_evidence_basis: The paper lists these as simulation service-time distributions but does not report an empirical fit procedure; treat as model inputs/assumptions.
data.limitations: Single ED; fit counts and method absent. Triangular specification is not an empirical quantile summary and cannot establish the actual distribution.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Use only as external assumed ranges for initial/follow-up consultation sensitivity scenarios; do not mix with measured means as if equally evidenced and do not transfer to RWJ.
